html:
The Takalak were an Aboriginal Australian people of inland north Queensland, in the upper Gilbert River country. The map shows them from 1600 to 1800.

Almost nothing is recorded of them beyond their name and territory. Neighbours on the map include the Agwamin, the Walangama and the Mayi Kulan. Gold finds on the Gilbert and Etheridge rivers from the late 1860s, and the cattle stations that came with them, took over the region within a few decades. See Aboriginal Australian societies.
